stories.article_text_excerpt: BRUSSELS — António Costa's EU budget tour is reaching the bigger capitals, with Berlin, Warsaw and Madrid on the agenda for the coming days. The settings may change, but the main question the European Council president is asking remains the same: Can we all agree on new EU taxes to help fund the long-term budget ? Introducing new EU-wide levies is crucial to lay the groundwork for a budget agreement by the end of the year, before national elections in France, Spain, Italy and Poland in 2027 threaten to disrupt the negotiations. Costa — who has been touring EU capitals to assess what each wants from the budget — will bring up the topic of taxes when he meets Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz on Wednesday. The following day, he will meet Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez in Madrid, along with Portugal’s Luís Montenegro in Lisbon. He will finish the week in Finland, meeting Prime Minister Petteri Orpo on Sunday. stories.title: Russia opens first road bridge with North Korea
stories.summary: Russia and North Korea have opened their first road bridge across the Tumen River as political, economic and military ties between the two countries deepen.
stories.article_text_excerpt: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5M4bT The new Russia-North Korea road bridge is named after Soviet Red Army officer Yakov Novichenko, who is credited with saving North Korean founder Kim Il Sung's life Image: Yuri Smityuk/TASS/picture alliance Advertisement Russia and North Korea on Monday cut the ribbon on the first road bridge linking the two countries as Moscow and Pyongyang deepen their strategic partnership. The crossing spans the Tumen River and marks another expansion of transport links between the two countries. Where is the new bridge? The road crossing is near the existing Friendship Bridge, a railway bridge commissioned in 1959 following the Korean War. Russia and North Korea already have direct rail and air connections, but until now there had been no road bridge between them. The new bridge is named after Soviet Red Army officer Yakov Novichenko, who is credited with saving North Korean founder Kim Il Sung's life. Relatives of Novichenko attended the opening ceremony. Nikolai Shcherbitsky and Tatyana Shcherbitskaya joined the ceremony to unveil the bridge named after their grandfather and father respectively Image: Yuri Smityu

stories.article_text_excerpt: BRUSSELS — The political reaction to the surge of migrants into the Spanish exclave of Ceuta laid bare how sharply Europe’s migration debate has shifted, and how it’s forcing migrant-rights groups to rethink the way they make their case. Where previous migration crises often divided European leaders between calls for solidarity and demands for tougher controls, the response to Ceuta — where more than 100 people died last month as they tried to enter — was strikingly uniform. From the far right to the center left, political leaders overwhelmingly called for stronger borders and more effective deterrence.
